decisions.scenario: Finding a Wednesday train from Kings Lynn to Cambridge after 11:45

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Can you help me find a train ticket for Wednesday?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Of course. What time would you like to leave, and where are you travelling from and to?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I need to leave after 11:45 from Kings Lynn and travel to Cambridge.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Train TR7040 leaves Kings Lynn at 12:11 and arrives in Cambridge at 12:58.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: How much does the trip cost?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: The fare is £9.80.

decisions.notes: Retained because the Wednesday Kings Lynn-to-Cambridge schedule, train ID TR7040, and £9.80 fare add source-backed route/day coverage not present in the reviewed corpus. The transient failed-search turn and unrelated unresolved restaurant tail are omitted.

decisions.scenario: Finding a Sunday train from Cambridge to London Kings Cross arriving before 21:30

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I'm looking for a train from Cambridge on Sunday.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: What is your destination, and what time do you need to arrive?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I need to go to London Kings Cross and arrive by 21:30.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: There is a train leaving Cambridge at 19:00 and arriving at London Kings Cross at 19:51.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: That works. I only needed the schedule, so I won't book it now.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: No problem. Have a good trip.

decisions.notes: Retained because the Sunday 19:00 Cambridge-to-London-Kings-Cross option and 19:51 arrival add a source-backed schedule distinct from existing Sunday coverage.

decisions.scenario: Finding an expensive seafood restaurant in central Cambridge

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I'm looking for an expensive restaurant in the city centre.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Do you have a preferred type of food?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: No. I just want an expensive place in the centre.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Loch Fyne is an expensive restaurant in the centre and is a good option.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: What kind of food does Loch Fyne serve?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Loch Fyne serves seafood.

decisions.notes: Retained because Loch Fyne and its expensive, central, seafood profile are source-backed facts not represented in the reviewed dialogue corpus. The unrelated unfinished train search is omitted.

decisions.scenario: Finding an expensive Indian restaurant in central Cambridge and getting its address

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Can you help me find an Indian restaurant in Cambridge?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Yes. What price range and part of town would you prefer?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I'd like an expensive restaurant in the centre.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Curry Garden is an expensive Indian restaurant in the centre.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Could you give me the address, please?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Curry Garden is at 106 Regent Street, City Centre.
